title: Scaling Instruction-Finetuned Language Models
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark measured the propensity of models to generate toxic text when prompted with sentences containing identity terms, including religious groups. This was evaluated by measuring the percentage and distribution of toxicity scores for model-generated continuations.
findings: Instruction finetuning reduces the overall generation of toxic language for prompts with religious identity terms compared to the base PaLM models. However, the finetuned Flan models still exhibit bias, mirroring patterns found in PaLM. Specifically, the upper quartile of toxicity scores for prompts related to Judaism was consistently higher than for other religious groups.
